title: Tool Manifest
description: Declares everything the engine needs to know about a tool: its identity, its inputs, its render target, and its capabilities. The template consumes inputs by name; this manifest declares them.

id.description: Stable, lowercase, hyphen-separated. NEVER changes once published. URL-safe.

extends.description: Brand-overlay marker - only valid on a tool inside a brand pack (brands/<brand>/tools/<id>/), never on a community tool. Declares this directory a per-file OVERLAY of the base pack's tool with the SAME id: scripts/use-profile.ts composes the profile view from community/<id>/ plus this dir (overlay file wins on filename collision, recursing one level into subdirs such as i18n/ and assets/) and strips this field from the composed tool.json, so shells and the engine never see it. The base community/<id>/tool.json must exist - a missing base fails the profile build loudly (never a silent partial tool). v1 supports only "community" as the base pack.

a11yLabel.description: Optional Handlebars template for the canvas's accessible label (the preview is exposed to screen readers as role=img). Hydrated live with input values, e.g. "QR code linking to {{url}}". Defaults to "<name> preview" when omitted.

version.description: SemVer. Bumped on any change. Used for cache-busting and saved-state migration.

engineVersion.description: SemVer range of engine versions this tool is compatible with, e.g. '^1.0.0'.

designVersion.description: Optional design-system version this tool renders against (plans/97 section 6a): a published version's slug, or 'latest' for the edit head. Author-controlled stability - a pinned tool keeps rendering against its version whatever gets republished. Unlike engineVersion this is NOT enforced at load: a pin naming a version this device does not have falls through to the active version, then to the head, so a tool always draws. Overridden per render by ?designv=. On a device that never published a version it has no effect at all.

status.description: Drives gallery sorting, watermarking, and brand-approval messaging. Experimental tools watermark their exports.

category.description: Free-form, used for gallery grouping. Examples: 'everyone', 'event', 'product', 'designer'.

new.description: Force the gallery's 'New' badge on this tool regardless of catalog position. Newness is otherwise inferred from catalog order (the most-recently-appended tools wear the badge and it self-expires as more ship); set this to keep a tool flagged new even after later tools push it out of that trailing window.

listed.description: Whether the tool appears in the gallery listing - the grid, search, favourites and the featured/utility strips (default true). Set false to UNLIST a tool that is a MECHANISM invoked from context rather than a destination the user browses to (e.g. asset-export, reached from the catalog's per-asset 'Download'). An unlisted tool still loads normally via #/tool/<id>, URL mode, and the CLI; unlisting only removes it from the gallery listing.

privacy.description: Marks an on-device utility - a tool that processes the user's OWN content (file in → transformed file out) entirely on the device, with nothing uploaded. The host shows a 'Runs on your device - nothing is uploaded' badge. Enforced conventions (validated): status must not be 'experimental' (no watermark on the user's own file) and the tool must not embed provenance metadata into the output. This is the marker for the privacy-flagship utility category (EXIF strip, redact, compress, convert) that replaces content exfiltration to single-purpose SaaS.

featured.description: Marks this tool for the gallery's cinematic 'Featured' hero row. Its presence (even {}) includes the tool; `variants` drive the tile's slow cross-fade between example inputs and themes. SUSE-specific curation lives here in the manifest (not in the open-source shell), so the featured row stays clean across the eventual repo split.

blurb.description: One-line end-user hook shown over the hero tile (sentence case, no period).

order.description: Optional sort key within the featured row (ascending). Entries without one sort after ordered ones, in catalog order.

variants.description: DEPRECATED alias for top-level `examples` - kept for tools authored before `examples` existed. When both are present, `examples` wins (in the featured row and the gallery tile). Prefer authoring `examples` (it also drives the gallery tile's preview strip).

examples.description: Example input value-sets that demonstrate the tool's range. They render live on the client (the same off-screen engine path an export takes) and are shown as the gallery tile's horizontally-scrollable preview strip - after the most-recent saved-session preview - and, when the tool is `featured`, as the hero row's cross-fade. Each is memoised so later visits are instant. Omit for a tool whose single committed preview says enough.

templates.description: Named starting points offered by the web shell's "New from template" chooser on a blank fresh open (no `?slot`, no URL values, no in-process seed, no `?template`). SOURCE OF TRUTH is the per-template files tools/<id>/templates/<tid>.json (each { id, name, category?, description?, thumb?, values }); build-catalog-index.ts scans that dir and the synced index carries METADATA ONLY (id/name/category/description/thumb) - the heavy `values` seed lives in the external file and is fetched on demand (chooser-select and the reserved `?template=<id>` launcher), never packed into the URL. This inline `templates[]` field is an OPTIONAL fallback for a tool that prefers inline metadata; when present the same items apply. Adding templates never changes a tool that lacks them, and never affects the manifest `default` composition (URL-mode / CLI / deep links still render with no chooser).

render.description: Defines the template render area and supported export formats.

formats.description: Output formats the tool supports. The host filters action buttons to these. Clipboard is an action (see render.actions), not a format.

denseSections.description: Section labels (input.section values) whose controls render in a denser 2-column grid instead of one control per row. A chrome-only presentation hint for input-dense pro tools; it never changes the input model, URL encoding, or determinism, and collapses back to one column on narrow panels/large-text. Wide controls (vector, blocks, textarea, asset, colour) still span the full width.

actions.description: Default actions to show. Defaults to ['copy', 'download', 'save'] if omitted.

export.description: Set false for utility/interactive tools that have no export. Hides download, copy, format, and dimension controls. Shows Save only when the tool has inputs. Hides the sidebar entirely when there are no inputs.

sidebar.description: Set false to declare inputs that are NOT presented as a left-panel sidebar: the inputs live only in the synced input model (URL params, collaboration, saved sessions, CLI/URL mode) and the tool's own template owns their editing UI. A full-bleed tool that still exports (render.export:true) keeps its export pill and canvas - the input aside is simply suppressed, exactly as for a no-input full-bleed tool. Use this for an interactive editor whose controls belong on the canvas (e.g. Run Web Code's code panes) rather than in a sidebar. Distinct from render.layout:'canvas' (which is for a single file drop-zone and forces export off) and from the chromeless 'editor'/'document' layouts (which keep a fixed render canvas).

layout.description: Presentation of the tool's interface. 'sidebar' (default) renders inputs in the left control panel. 'canvas' hides the sidebar and presents the tool as a full-bleed working area - a single declared 'file' input is shown as a drag-and-drop / click-to-pick zone on the canvas itself (for on-device file utilities). 'editor' hides the sidebar too, but keeps the fixed-size render canvas AND the full render/export controls (render pill + export popup): a chromeless WYSIWYG surface. A tool using 'editor' declares one 'blocks' input carrying a `canvas` flag (which maps its geometry fields); the web shell mounts a direct-manipulation overlay (select / drag / resize / rotate / z-order / align / distribute) that reads and writes that flat blocks array. Data stays flat and URL-expressible, so CLI/URL mode render the same artwork with no overlay. Input semantics are unchanged. 'document' is a chromeless multi-page flowing-document surface (paged tools): it keeps the render/export controls like 'editor' but mounts a rich-text document editor (on-canvas format ribbon, per-block controls, contenteditable, rich-HTML paste) over a 'blocks' input whose rows are content blocks (heading/text/lolly/table). Pagination lives in the tool's hook, so CLI/URL render the same document with no editor. 'deck' is a slide-deck editor: it KEEPS the input sidebar (not chromeless) and mounts a live on-canvas overlay (deck-editor.js) over a 'blocks' input whose rows are slides - click a slide to edit its text/colour/images in place, navigate a thumbnail rail. Bounded DOM: an edit-mode hook render-mode shows one active slide plus tiny thumbnails, and the overlay restores a full-deck render before export.

dims.description: Set false to hide the export dimension inputs in the download bar.

units.description: Set false to offer pixels only - hides the physical-unit (mm/cm/in/pt) selector and the DPI field in the download bar. Width/height stay in px, so an on-screen pixel is an exported pixel. Use for tools whose output is inherently pixel-measured (screen assets, favicons, token-cost images) where a physical print size is meaningless and would make width/height inputs disagree with the true raster resolution.

paginate.description: Engine-driven pagination. `source` names a `table` input whose rows each produce one page: the runtime hydrates the template once per row (with a `page` context object: index/number/count, `first` = the row's first cell, `cells` = [{column, value}], `fields` = cells minus the first) and wraps each hydration in its own [data-pdf-page] box. The tool authors ONE page and never manages pagination itself. Pair with `paged: true` for the scrolling all-pages canvas + filmstrip.

paged.description: Marks a multi-page document tool - one whose output lays out several `[data-pdf-page]` boxes (e.g. multi-page-pdf). The gallery renders each page as its own horizontally-scrollable preview slide (via renderToolPages) instead of input-variant example looks.

filmstrip.description: Which edge the paged tool's slide-sorter filmstrip runs along. `left` (the default) is a vertical rail beside the canvas - right for tall documents. `bottom` is the deck-strip shape, for tools whose pages are wide and few (cards, slides), where a left rail would eat the width the page needs. Only read when `paged: true`.

pages.description: Turns an `editor`-layout tool into a MULTI-PAGE canvas (carousel-maker): the web shell sizes `#tool-canvas` to a horizontal strip of N same-size page frames (fit-to-single-page off) and the free-canvas overlay places boxes across all frames. Box coordinates stay a single flat, global, URL-expressible array; the tool's hook derives which page each box belongs to (by centre) and emits one `[data-pdf-page]` frame per page, so headless CLI/URL render identically and export fans out (multi-page PDF, or one still image per page). Requires `layout:'editor'` and `paged:true`. Values name the input ids the page geometry is read from, so the shell stays generic.

count.description: Input id (a number input) holding the page count. Clamped to [min, max].

width.description: Input id (a number input, px) holding each page's width. All pages share it.

height.description: Input id (a number input, px) holding each page's height. All pages share it.

gap.description: Gap in px between page frames in the editor strip. MUST equal the tool template/hook's own frame gap so overlay handles and rendered boxes stay aligned.

printMarks.description: Set false to hide the 'Print marks & bleed' card from the download bar. The print-finishing path (crop/registration marks, bleed box, page boxes) applies to a single trim-sized artwork, so multi-page documents (which emit per-page boxes) opt out of it. Set true to DECLARE PRINT INTENT: the card's master toggle then defaults ON for every print-capable format. Left unset, the card is offered but starts OFF for the RGB vector formats (pdf/svg/eps) and ON only for the separating press formats (pdf-cmyk/cmyk-tiff/eps-cmyk) - marks and bleed are never a side effect of picking a physical unit or an everyday PDF/SVG.

transparentBg.description: Adds a 'No BG' (transparent background) toggle to the export bar. The engine injects it into the model so hooks can react to it via onInit/onInput.

c2pa.description: Whether the Content Credentials (C2PA) toggle is pre-checked in the export panel. Default TRUE - every tool stamps a signed provenance manifest by default (for the C2PA-capable formats it exports). Set FALSE to opt a tool out. Ignored (forced off) for privacy:'on-device' tools, which must never embed provenance into a user's own file. A ?c2pa= link/save value overrides this per export.

liveMaxEdge.description: For onFrame (live camera) tools only: the requested longest edge, in pixels, of the working camera frame handed to the hook. The shell downscales the source camera to a small default that suits a vector trace; a raster-output tool (whose result is a bitmap, not traced shapes - e.g. pixel-stretch) sets this higher for sharper output. The shell clamps it to the native camera frame (never upscales) and to its own ceiling. Ignored by tools without onFrame and by shells without a camera.

liveMaxEdgeInput.description: For onFrame (live camera) tools: id of a number input whose value overrides liveMaxEdge, exposing camera resolution as a user-facing control (e.g. a slider). The runtime reads it at go-live and re-applies to the running stream whenever the input changes - no camera stop/start - so the working frame resolution follows the control. Falls back to liveMaxEdge when the input is unset or absent.

liveDefault.description: For onFrame tools: catalog id of an ANIMATED SVG asset the shell plays as a live, no-camera source (an off-screen of the animation, sampled into onFrame like a camera would be) so the tool can show off its effect on a moving subject without a webcam. The shell auto-plays it when present; a still export still captures the current frame. Ignored by tools without onFrame.

convertPaths.description: Controls the 'Convert paths' export toggle (outline text to vector paths in SVG/PDF/PDF-CMYK so output renders identically without the fonts installed). The engine auto-injects the toggle whenever the tool exports a vector format. Set false to suppress the toggle entirely and never outline text - e.g. capture tools, where the output is a raster and text-outlining doesn't apply.

preview.description: Marks a tool whose live canvas is a placeholder until an explicit, expensive render runs (e.g. a capture tool that screenshots a page in beforeExport). The shell wires a [data-preview] control in the template to render into the frame - preview only, never a download - and re-shows the placeholder whenever an input changes (the last preview is invalidated).

format.description: Format used for the preview render. Defaults to the tool's first render format. Pick a cheap raster (e.g. webp) - the blob is discarded; only the painted frame is kept.

auto.description: Generate a preview automatically once the tool finishes loading, so the user lands on a rendered frame rather than the placeholder. Fires once on load only - never on every input change - so deferred renders stay deliberate.

video.description: Default video capture settings used when webm or mp4 is in formats.

wait.description: Seconds to wait before recording starts. Default 1.

duration.description: Length of the recorded clip in seconds. Default 5.

capture.description: Marks a device-recording tool (requires host.recorder + the matching 'microphone'/'camera' capability). Tells the shell which record affordance to mount: 'audio' = mic-only (a voice recorder - also shows a live level meter when the tool declares an onLevel hook); 'video' = camera-only, SILENT (no mic track); 'av' = camera+mic (a talking-head/video recorder - use this, not 'video', when the clip needs sound, and declare BOTH 'camera' and 'microphone'; the shell also shows an audio-level + background-noise coaching HUD). 'screen' = display capture (requires the 'screen' capability): the shell mounts a Screenshot + Record pair and the browser's own picker chooses the screen/window/tab, so the tool never names or sees a target it wasn't handed. Absent = no record button. The recorded bytes reach the user via the transform path (host.export.file, never watermarked) or, for a compositing tool, become a template asset the render wraps.

aspectWarning.description: Editor-only guard for tools whose layout only suits a certain orientation (e.g. a portrait-only document). Shows a prominent warning beside the dimension controls when the current page aspect ratio (width ÷ height) falls outside [min, max]. Never affects - or appears in - the rendered/exported output.

min.description: Minimum acceptable aspect ratio (width ÷ height). Below this, the warning shows. Omit to leave the low end unbounded.

max.description: Maximum acceptable aspect ratio (width ÷ height). Above this, the warning shows. Omit to leave the high end unbounded.

message.description: The warning text shown to the editor.

inputs.description: Declares user-facing inputs. The host generates UI from this. The template references inputs by id.

capabilities.description: Declares what host capabilities this tool needs. The host disables the tool on shells that can't provide them (e.g. an ffmpeg-using tool is unavailable in the web shell; a 'microphone'/'camera'/'screen' recording tool is unavailable in the headless CLI). 'screen' (v1.54) is DISPLAY capture via host.recorder - the user picks a screen/window/tab in browser-native UI; distinct from 'capture', which rasterises a URL the tool itself names.

network.description: Configuration for the 'network' capability: which URLs host.net.fetch may reach. Only meaningful alongside capabilities:["network"]. Fail-closed - without this block (or for a URL no entry matches) every host.net fetch rejects.

allowlist.description: https URLs the host permits. A trailing /* makes an entry a prefix wildcard ("https://api.example.com/*" allows everything under that path); the wildcard must follow a path separator, so a prefix can never bleed into a lookalike host ("https://api.example.com*" would also match https://api.example.com.evil.io/). Without it the entry allows that exact URL only. The same matching rules apply on every shell.

composes.description: Nested renders (tool composition). Each entry renders another tool's output to an embeddable asset, exposed to the template as an extra referenced via {{asset <id>}} (so a logic-less template can embed one tool's render inside another). Requires the 'compose' capability. Recursion is depth- and cycle-guarded by the host. Capped (maxItems) well under the render cache so a single tool's composes can't self-evict mid-render.

id.description: Name the composed asset is exposed under. Reference it in the template as {{asset <id>}}; guard with {{#if <id>}} since composition can fail gracefully.

tool.description: id of the tool to render.

inputs.description: Inputs passed to the composed tool, keyed by the child tool's input ids. String values are Handlebars, hydrated against THIS tool's own context (its input values + extras), so child inputs can bind to parent values, e.g. { "url": "{{url}}" }.

format.description: Render format for the composed output. Default: svg when the child supports it (vector embeds stay crisp in svg/pdf exports), else png.

width.description: Render width in px. Defaults to the composed tool's native width.

height.description: Render height in px. Defaults to the composed tool's native height.

guide.description: A short 'how do I actually use the thing I just made' walkthrough, shown as a dialog behind a help button beside the tool's title (web shell) and opened once automatically on a device's first visit to the tool. For the last mile a render can't teach on its own - where the export goes and what to do with it there. Keep it to a handful of steps: it is a nudge, not documentation (link to docs from a step for the long version). Translatable via the tool's i18n sidecar under `guide.*`.

title.description: Dialog heading. Defaults to a generic 'How to use it' in the shell when omitted.

tracks.description: One track per route the user might take (e.g. desktop vs phone). A single track renders as a plain step list; two or more render as tabs.

id.description: Stable key for this track - the i18n sidecar path (`guide.tracks.<id>.…`) is built from it, so treat it like an input id.

label.description: Tab label. Keep it to one or two words.

steps.description: Ordered steps, rendered as a numbered list. Plain text - `**bold**` is the only markup, for naming the control being pointed at.

note.description: Optional closing caveat under the steps (e.g. what this route cannot do).

hooks.description: Optional escape hatch. If present, the tool ships a hooks.js file that the host loads in a sandboxed context.

onFrame.description: The tool reacts to a live camera stream. When the shell provides host.media (a camera) the runtime drives this hook once per frame with { frame, model, host }, where frame is { width, height, data (RGBA), t }; the returned patch updates the render exactly like onInit/onInput. Pure progressive enhancement - the tool still runs as a still-image tool where no camera is available, so it must NOT be declared as a required 'camera' capability.

onLevel.description: The tool reacts to live audio levels while metering/recording (e.g. a mic recorder's VU meter + coaching). When the shell provides host.recorder the runtime drives this hook per level sample with { level, model, host }, where level is { rms, peak, dbfs, clipping, t }; the returned patch updates the render like onFrame (drop-overlap, not time-boxed). The tool declares the 'microphone' capability, so - unlike onFrame - it only runs where a mic can be recorded.

exportFile.description: The tool produces output via the transform path (file in → transformed file out) rather than rasterising the DOM. The hook reads the picked file's bytes (input.value.bytes) and returns a { bytes, mime, filename } record; the host wraps it in a Blob and delivers it via host.export.file (no watermark, no embedded provenance). A batch tool (a `multiple` file input) may instead return an ARRAY of such records - one per file - which the host delivers as a single zip. Used by on-device utilities.

exportStill.description: The tool owns a raster still export at a bit depth the 8-bit DOM raster cannot originate (16-bit/HDR PNG, OpenEXR, Radiance). The runtime calls this hook (engine 1.100+) before host.export.render with { node, format, opts (depth/hdr/width/height/dpi), host }; returning { bytes, mime } short-circuits the export to those bytes (via host.codec, computed in float), while returning null declines and falls through to the normal path for that format. Tool-supplied bytes carry no watermark or engine provenance.

isolate.description: Opt this tool's hooks into a Worker-isolated execution context (engine 1.105+, plans/86-worker-isolation-hooks.md M2) instead of the default in-realm 'new Function' path. Set only once hooks.js is verified never to touch DOM globals (document/window/Image/canvas); a shell without a Worker-backed executor silently runs the tool in-realm, so declaring it is always safe (a hint, not a hard requirement).

id.description: Referenced in the template as {{id}}. Also becomes a URL param.

notice.description: Always-visible fine print rendered above the control (unlike help, which sits behind an info button). For what the user should read before typing - e.g. the consent disclosure on an input whose value triggers a network lookup.

bindToProfile.description: If set, pre-fills from the user profile field of this name (e.g. 'firstname', 'headshot'). User can override.

bindToMeta.description: If set, this input's value is embedded into the export's provenance metadata (EXIF/XMP/PNG text + the C2PA manifest) under this field, overriding the profile-derived default. 'copyright' and 'license' are user-asserted IP fields with no profile source (see the embed-track-image tool).

matchExportFormat.description: For an asset/file input: the default export format follows this input's uploaded format (a dropped JPEG defaults the export to jpg) until the user picks a format. The uploaded format must be one the tool's render.formats offers, else the first format is used.

group.description: Optional grouping tag. The reserved value 'export' moves an input out of the sidebar into the export panel; the engine injects its own export-group toggles (transparentBg, convertPaths). Any other value is a free-form label for related controls.

showIf.description: Conditional visibility: the input renders in the sidebar only while every { otherInputId: value } pair here matches the current model (e.g. { "vectorize": true }).

attachTo.description: Id of a sibling input. Renders THIS input's control inside that input's control row (leading) instead of on its own labelled row - for a compact modifier belonging to another control, e.g. a fit toggle on an asset slot. It stays an ordinary input everywhere else (URL params, hooks, state, undo); only its placement changes. Pair with display:'icon-toggle' to keep it to one button. Ignored if the target id does not exist.

dataSource.description: Adds a unified 'Add data' affordance to this input: the user picks a file (csv/json/txt/md/xlsx) or a catalog text/boilerplate asset, and its content fills the field. For a text/longtext input the content is applied as text (an .xlsx is serialised to CSV, first sheet). Replaces per-tool paste buttons / 'paste your CSV here' instructions. See plan 87.

tags.description: Catalog text-asset tags to offer from the library, AND-matched. Default ["boilerplate"].

accept.description: Override the file-input accept filter (default covers csv/json/txt/md/xlsx).

rangeWhen.description: Conditional slider bounds: the first entry whose `when` map matches the current model overrides min/max/step (e.g. per-mode limits). Drives the web slider UI only - a tool that must enforce the bound elsewhere (URL/CLI values are not auto-clamped) does so in a hook.

palette.description: Asset ID of a palette asset to constrain choices. If omitted, free color picker.

swatchesOnly.description: Restrict to brand palette swatches only - hides the hex entry, native picker and alpha. Default false (full picker).

display.description: 'icon-toggle' renders the select as ONE compact button that cycles its options, showing the current option's `icon` instead of a dropdown. Intended for 2-state modifiers (with attachTo); a longer option list still cycles, but a dropdown reads better past ~3. 'segmented' renders the options as a row of side-by-side tabs (a radiogroup) instead of a dropdown - for a small, mutually-exclusive mode switch (2–4 options) like Hue/Saturation/Luminance; past ~4 a dropdown reads better.

icon.description: Icon name from the web shell's registry (shells/web/src/lib/icons.ts), shown instead of the label when display is 'icon-toggle'. Falls back to the label if the name is unknown.

badge.description: Short pill shown beside this option's label. If ANY option carries a badge, the web shell renders the select as a badged picker (a radiogroup of labelled pills) instead of a native dropdown - so the badge is visible while choosing, not only after. For discovery/evaluation hints, e.g. 'vector' / 'raster' on a filter-effect picker. Keep it to one short word.

formats.description: Export formats to offer while THIS option is selected - a subset of render.formats. Lets one select (e.g. an effect picker) drive the export format bar so each choice offers only the formats it produces well, while render.formats stays the union. Intersected with the tool's render.formats and the device's capability filter. Ignored unless the shell wires the option to the format bar.

width.description: Export width this option implies, in `unit`. With `height`, selecting the option sets the export dimensions (so a 'size' select drives the printed page size). The shell applies it to the export bar; the user can still override.

height.description: Export height this option implies, in `unit`.

unit.description: Unit for this option's width/height. Defaults to 'mm' when width/height are present.

filter.description: Constraints passed to host.assets.query(). Limits the picker.

allowUpload.description: If true, picker offers user upload alongside library.

accept.description: Allowlist of accepted file types - MIME types and/or extensions (e.g. ["image/jpeg", "image/png", ".heic"]). Used as the file picker's `accept` attribute. Empty/omitted accepts any file. This is a UX hint, not a security boundary - the hook should still validate bytes.

maxSize.description: Maximum accepted file size in bytes. The host rejects larger files at pick time. Omit for no limit.

multiple.description: Accept MANY files at once (batch tools). The input's value becomes an array of loaded files instead of a single one, the web file-picker sets the `multiple` attribute, and the CLI collects repeated --<id>=path occurrences. An `exportFile` hook may then return one { bytes, mime, filename } record per file (the host delivers them as a single zip). See the embed-track tool.

addMenu.description: Turns the '+ Add' button into a typed menu. Each option of the named discriminator sub-field becomes a menu entry; an entry already used is disabled unless its option sets repeatable:true. The discriminator is fixed at creation and shown as the block's label rather than an editable control.

field.description: id of the select sub-field whose options drive the menu.

labelledFields.description: Show a text label above each sub-field (the layout typed/addMenu blocks always use). Turn on for untyped blocks whose controls aren't self-evident, or that carry several optional fields.

rowActions.description: Add copy / paste / clear buttons to each block's header (next to collapse + remove): copy a row's values, paste them onto another row to make the two match, or clear a row to its field defaults. Useful when rows are many-field states people want to duplicate (e.g. flythrough poses).

fields.description: Sub-fields for each repeatable block entry. A field may declare a `type` (text|color|select|asset|number|boolean); text is the default. `showFor` limits a field to blocks whose discriminator value is listed; `showIf` limits it by sibling-field and/or top-level input values.

default.description: Value a newly-added block's field starts at.

help.description: Short hint shown under the sub-field (labelledFields blocks only).

showFor.description: Render this field only when the block's discriminator value is one of these.

showIf.description: Render this field only when the named values all match. Keys are looked up first among sibling fields of the same block, then among top-level input ids (e.g. { "vectorize": true, "tune": true }).

multilineFor.description: Render a text field as a multi-line textarea (rather than a single-line input) when the block's discriminator value is one of these.

rows.description: Visible rows for a multi-line text field (see multilineFor). Default 3.

options.description: Choices for a select sub-field. An option's repeatable:true lets the add-menu offer it more than once.

optionsFrom.description: Render this sub-field as a reference picker whose choices are the rows of another blocks input (or several). The stored value is each target row's derived id (slug of its key field, else its label, else an ordinal) - the same id a tool's hook resolves - so it replaces hand-typed ID cross-references with a dropdown. A stored value matching no current row is surfaced as an '(unknown)' option rather than silently dropped.

input.description: id of the blocks input to draw rows from (single-source form).

value.description: Source-row sub-field used as the stored id (slugged + de-duplicated to match the tool's resolution).

label.description: Source-row sub-field shown to the user (falls back to the derived id).

prefix.description: Ordinal id prefix for rows with neither key nor label.

sources.description: Several source inputs merged into one option list (e.g. cards AND layers). De-duplicated by value, first wins.

freeText.description: Render as a combobox (datalist) that also accepts a typed value not in the list - e.g. a kanban column invented on the spot.

excludeSelf.description: Omit the current row from its own options (a card can't be its own parent).

excludeDescendants.description: Omit the current row's descendants (requires the input's `nesting`) so a node can't reparent into its own subtree.

emptyLabel.description: Label for the blank/none option (default '- none -').

nesting.description: Treat this blocks array as an editable TREE: the sidebar renders it as an indented outline and the header drag lets a card be dropped above, below, or INSIDE another, updating the dragged card's parent reference (its whole subtree travels with it). The data stays a flat reference-by-id array - only the presentation is tree-shaped - so it serialises and renders exactly as before.

parentField.description: Sub-field holding each row's parent reference (the id of another row).

keyField.description: Sub-field used as a row's id (what parentField points at).

labelField.description: Fallback id source when keyField is blank, and the human label for indentation.

prefix.description: Ordinal id prefix for rows with neither key nor label.

activeWhen.description: Only treat the input as a tree when these top-level input values match (an array value matches by membership), e.g. { "diagramType": ["org", "mindmap"] }. Omit to always nest.

dropToAdd.description: Turns the blocks list into a drop zone: dragging or selecting several image files at once creates one block per file, each with the file uploaded into the named asset sub-field. Every other field of a new block starts at its declared default.

field.description: id of the block's `asset` sub-field that each dropped file is uploaded into.

accept.description: MIME accept filter for dropped files (default "image/*"). A trailing /* matches a whole type group.

mdPaste.description: Adds a 'Paste Markdown' button to the blocks toolbar. It reads the clipboard, splits the Markdown into one block per heading (the heading line → the block's `heading` field, the section beneath it → its `body` field, kept as Markdown for the tool's {{markdown}} render), and appends the blocks - so a whole document lands as editable, page-flowing blocks. A block gets kind:'text' when the input has a `kind` discriminator; other fields start at their defaults.

importData.description: Lets the user populate the whole list from a CSV or JSON file (the ingest counterpart to CSV/JSON export). The shell offers an 'Import data' control; the engine (parseDataRows) maps columns onto these fields - by explicit `columns` map, else by matching each column header/key case-insensitively to a field's id then its label - and sets the input value. Data stays flat and serialises exactly like hand-entered blocks.

formats.description: Accepted data formats. Defaults to both csv and json.

mode.description: Whether an import replaces the current rows or appends to them. Default replace.

columns.description: Explicit fieldId → source column/key overrides. Omit to auto-map by header (field id, then label). e.g. { "value": "Amount" }.

canvas.description: Marks this blocks array as a free-form WYSIWYG canvas of positioned 'boxes' (requires render.layout:'editor'). The web shell mounts a direct-manipulation overlay - select, drag, resize, rotate, re-stack (z-order = array order, later rows paint on top), align and distribute - that reads and writes this flat array through the normal input path. The fields named below give the overlay the geometry to manipulate; every field remains an ordinary block sub-field, so the layout stays flat, URL-expressible, and renders identically headless (CLI/URL) with no overlay. Field ORDER in `fields` is the compact-URL wire format - never reorder or remove once shipped. CLOSED SET: unknown keys are rejected, because a typo'd `*Field` name is silently inert at runtime (the overlay reads a field nothing writes) - so the schema, not a bug report, has to catch it. Every `*Field` value must also name a real sub-field id in the SIBLING `fields` array; scripts/validate-catalog.ts enforces that half. Adding a key here is therefore a BREAKING change for older shells: the same schema is what engine/src/loader.ts validates a manifest against at load time, so a manifest carrying a key an older engine's copy does not list is refused whole, not partially ignored. Ship a new canvas key together with an `engineVersion` floor that names the engine which introduced it - the loader checks that range BEFORE validating, so an old shell reports the version, not a schema error.

idField.description: Sub-field holding each box's stable id (used to track selection across re-stacking). Default 'id'.

xField.description: Number sub-field: box left, in canvas (native render) pixels. Default 'x'.

yField.description: Number sub-field: box top, in canvas pixels. Default 'y'.

wField.description: Number sub-field: box width, in canvas pixels. Default 'w'.

hField.description: Number sub-field: box height, in canvas pixels. Default 'h'.

rotationField.description: Number sub-field: clockwise rotation in degrees about the box centre. Default 'rot'.

radiusField.description: Number sub-field: corner radius in px (used when shape is rounded).

fillField.description: Color sub-field: box background fill (empty = transparent).

gradField.description: Text sub-field: a gradient fill as a Lolly gradient spec (kind_angle_colour-pos_colour-pos, e.g. lin_90_30ba78-0_efefef-100). Painted OVER the flat fill, so a translucent stop composites onto it; empty = no gradient. The hook lowers it through host.color.gradientCss, so an engine that predates that primitive degrades to the flat fill.

imageField.description: Asset sub-field: image drawn inside the box.

fitField.description: Select sub-field: how the image fills the box (object-fit: cover/contain/fill).

imgPosField.description: Select sub-field: CSS object-position anchor (which edge/corner a contained image sits against, or which part of a cover-cropped image stays in frame). Honoured in raster + SVG (preserveAspectRatio) + PDF export.

blendField.description: Select sub-field: CSS mix-blend-mode for the whole box (faithful in raster export; flattened in vector).

textField.description: Text sub-field: text drawn inside the box.

fontSizeField.description: Number sub-field: text size in px.

padField.description: Number sub-field: inner padding in px between the box edge and its text.

fitTextField.description: Boolean sub-field: shrink the text until it fits inside the box (shrink-ONLY - never larger than the authored size). Off = the box is expected to grow to its text instead.

groupField.description: Text sub-field: id of the group this box belongs to (empty = ungrouped). Boxes sharing a group id move / scale / rotate together; purely an editor concept (no render effect).

clipField.description: Text sub-field: id of another box whose shape clips this one (a clip-path mask). Faithful in raster + SVG export; flattened in PDF/EMF.

pathField.description: Text sub-field holding a VECTOR path box's authored path - the pen tool's own form (nodes + handles + spline kind), encoded as one delimiter-safe value by host.geom.encodeAuthored. Node coordinates are NORMALISED to the box frame (fractions of w/h, values outside 0..1 legal), so the ordinary move / resize / rotate gestures act on a path box through x/y/w/h/rot without rewriting a single node. Machine-written and machine-read only: the field carries showFor:[] so it never renders as a sidebar control. The tool's hook lowers it via host.geom.fromNodes and emits an inline <svg><path>, which vector-exports with no extra export code.

strokeField.description: Color sub-field: stroke paint for a path/box/image outline (empty = no stroke). Defaults to 'stroke' when the canvas omits it, so the overlay and the vector operations read the same sub-field.

strokeWField.description: Number sub-field: stroke width in canvas px. Default 'strokeW'.

fillRuleField.description: Select sub-field: a path's fill rule - nonzero or evenodd. Default 'fillRule'.

strokeDashField.description: Select sub-field: dash STYLE as a keyword ('' solid / dashed / dotted). The pattern is derived from the stroke width so it keeps its proportions when the width changes; an authored `strokeDashArrayField` wins over it. Default 'strokeDash'.

strokeCapField.description: Select sub-field: line cap - round, butt or square. Default 'strokeCap'.

strokeJoinField.description: Select sub-field: line join - round, miter or bevel. Default 'strokeJoin'.

strokeDashArrayField.description: Text sub-field: an AUTHORED dash pattern as SPACE-separated numbers in stroke-width units ("6 4" = a 6-long dash, a 4-long gap). A string, not a list, and space-separated rather than comma-separated, because one block sub-field is one scalar and a comma would split the compact blocks URL row. Set, it wins over the `strokeDashField` keyword. Default 'strokeDashArray'.

dashFitField.description: Boolean sub-field: stretch the authored dash pattern slightly so a whole number of dashes fits between each corner and each end of the path (Illustrator's corner-aligned dashes) instead of a half dash landing on a corner. Applied by the tool's hook. Default 'dashFit'.

headStartField.description: Select sub-field: the decoration drawn at the path's FIRST point, along that end's own tangent - none · triangle · open · circle · diamond · bar. Same vocabulary as the connector heads, because a spline, a line and a connector are one primitive carrying one decoration set. Default 'headStart'.

headEndField.description: Select sub-field: the same decoration at the path's LAST point. Default 'headEnd'.

bindStartField.description: Text sub-field: the id of the box this path's FIRST point is attached to, '' for a free end. Machine-written by the bind gesture (carries showFor:[]), never typed; a bound end is what hands the path to connector routing. Default 'bindStart'.

bindEndField.description: Text sub-field: the same binding for the path's LAST point. Default 'bindEnd'.

routeField.description: Select sub-field: how a path with a BOUND end routes between its boxes (straight, elbow-*, curved-*, arc-*). '' = auto, read off the path's own spline kind - the explicit value exists because six spline kinds cannot name the engine's thirteen routes. Default 'route'.

pathLayerClass.description: Class the tool's hook puts on its committed BOUND-PATH <svg> layer. The overlay hides that layer for the duration of a drag so the live preview doesn't double up with the stale committed one - only the manifest knows what its own hook emits. Default 'lolly-connectors'.

shadowField.description: SELECT sub-field (not a Boolean - a shadow has a target, and the value names it): 'none' · 'box' (the frame's own silhouette, a box-shadow) · 'text' (the type only, a text-shadow) · 'content' (the artwork's alpha silhouette, a filter: drop-shadow). The vocabulary is additive: a depth-capable tool may extend it with 'depth', whose offset/blur are DERIVED from the box's `zField` rather than authored. Whatever the value, the x/y/blur/colour sub-fields below supply the geometry.

shadowXField.description: Number sub-field: drop-shadow x offset in px.

shadowYField.description: Number sub-field: drop-shadow y offset in px.

shadowBlurField.description: Number sub-field: drop-shadow blur radius in px.

zField.description: Number sub-field: the box's DEPTH - how far it sits in front of (positive) or behind (negative) the stage plane, in canvas px. Layers stay parallel to the screen, so a camera turns z into a per-layer uniform scale + translate (parallax, push-in, depth-of-field) and the render stays affine end-to-end. Absent field or 0 = the flat, unlifted board; the authored slider runs 0–300 and the value clamps to −300…900.

startField.description: Number sub-field: when this box appears, in SECONDS from the start of the sequence. Empty = the box is 'scenery' (always visible). Timing is inert unless a shell mounts a timeline panel; static exports ignore it.

durField.description: Number sub-field: how long the box stays visible, in SECONDS. Empty = runs to the end of the sequence.

clipInField.description: Number sub-field: trim in-point WITHIN the box's own media (video/lottie/audio), in SECONDS from the media's start. Ignored for non-media boxes.

speedField.description: Number sub-field: media playback rate multiplier (1 = normal). Affects how much source media a given timeline duration consumes.

enterField.description: Select sub-field: named animate-in preset played at the box's start (e.g. fade, rise, pop; 'none' disables). Presets are shell-rendered; no keyframes are authored.

exitField.description: Select sub-field: named animate-out preset played at the box's end (e.g. fade, rise, pop; 'none' disables). Presets are shell-rendered; no keyframes are authored.

enterMsField.description: Number sub-field: duration of the enter preset, in MILLISECONDS.

exitMsField.description: Number sub-field: duration of the exit preset, in MILLISECONDS.

enterEaseField.description: String sub-field: the timing curve the enter preset's GEOMETRY follows - a preset name (linear, ease-out, ease-in, ease-in-out, overshoot, anticipate) or a CSS cubic-bezier(a,b,c,d). Empty = the preset's own built-in curve. Opacity is deliberately not governed by it: a fade that tracks a slow curve turns to mud under video compression, so alpha keeps its fixed ramp.

exitEaseField.description: String sub-field: the same curve control for the exit preset. Same wire format, same geometry-only reach.

muteField.description: Boolean sub-field: silence this box's own audio track when the sequence is mixed.

linkField.description: String sub-field: the id of the box this one is A/V-linked to (written on BOTH sides when audio is detached from a video). Absent or naming a missing box reads as unlinked.

laneField.description: Select sub-field: '' places the box on a free overlay lane; 'seq' places it on the magnetic main sequence row, where clips are kept gapless and edits ripple.

kfField.description: Text sub-field: the box's KEYFRAME TRACK - its whole authored animation as one compact, delimiter-safe string (times in ms, per-channel values at the pinned quanta, per-segment easing). Machine-written by the timeline, so the sub-field carries showFor:[] and never renders as a sidebar control. Absent or empty = the box is not keyframed and every keyframe path is inert for it.

frameField.description: Text sub-field: the id of the FRAME (page/artboard container) box this box belongs to; '' = it sits on the open board. Declaring it turns on the frame primitive - the overlay drives gestures in frame-local space via each frame's DOM offset, and re-buckets a moved/created/resized box into whichever frame its centre lands in on drop. Absent leaves every frame-aware path dead (byte-identical to a frameless editor).

frameKind.description: NOT a field name: the literal `kind` VALUE that marks a box as a frame rather than ordinary content (e.g. 'frame'). Frames render as free-placed [data-pdf-page] pages at their authored x/y.

orderField.description: Number sub-field on a FRAME box: its page order in a multi-page export. Read by the tool's hook; the overlay's frame-reorder control writes it. Absent = no reorder affordance.

clipChildrenField.description: Boolean sub-field on a FRAME box: whether content overflowing the frame is clipped to it. Absent = the overlay offers no clip toggle.

minSize.description: Smallest box width/height the overlay will create or resize to, in canvas px. Default 8.

addKinds.description: The kinds of box the 'add' tool offers. Each entry seeds a new box's fields (id excluded - the shell assigns it).

id.description: Kind id (also the default select value of the shape/kind field if present).

icon.description: Optional inline SVG or glyph for the menu entry.

seed.description: Field values a newly-added box of this kind starts at (merged over the block's declared defaults).

import.description: Opt into design-file IMPORT on this canvas: the editor's Lolly menu gains an 'Import a design' entry that maps an imported file's frames/shapes onto boxes of THIS array, using the tool's own font-select values and addKinds seed colours so the result is indistinguishable from natively-authored boxes. Absent (Design's historical state) = no import control at all.

formats.description: The design formats this canvas advertises accepting (today: svg, penpot, pdf, ai, idml). Documents intent for the import panel; the engine's importer is the authority on what it can actually parse.

mode.description: 'scenes' (Sequence Studio): an imported design's frames land as timed clips APPENDED to the main sequence instead of replacing the canvas. Requires the full time model to be mapped; omit for editors whose import replaces the board.

connect.description: Opt into connector authoring (Org Chart): a SECOND blocks input holding {from,to} edges between boxes, plus a 'Connect' rail mode to author them (click a source card, then targets). The overlay reads/writes that array and draws a live preview; the tool's hooks.js owns the real routed geometry. Absent = the editor's toolbar and gestures are unchanged.

input.description: id of the blocks input storing the connector edges. Its sub-fields - not this canvas's `fields` - are what the *Field names below refer to.

fromField.description: Edge sub-field holding the SOURCE box id. Default 'from'.

toField.description: Edge sub-field holding the TARGET box id. Default 'to'.

styleField.description: Edge sub-field: route style (elbow, straight, curved …).

arrowField.description: Edge sub-field: which ENDS carry an arrowhead (none/end/both).

headField.description: Edge sub-field: arrowhead SHAPE (triangle/open/circle/diamond/bar) - same vocabulary as the path decorations.

widthField.description: Edge sub-field: line width in canvas px.

layerClass.description: Class of the tool's rendered connector <svg>, hidden mid-drag so the live preview doesn't double up with the committed one. Default 'oc-connectors'.

defaultStyle.description: Route style a newly-authored edge starts at. Default 'elbow'.

defaultArrow.description: Arrow ends a newly-authored edge starts at. Default 'end'.

defaultHead.description: Arrowhead shape a newly-authored edge starts at. Default 'triangle'.

defaultColor.description: Line colour a newly-authored edge starts at. Default '#94a3b8'.

defaultWidth.description: Line width a newly-authored edge starts at. Default 2.5.

grid.description: Opt into snap-to-grid: the overlay rounds drag/resize to this lattice (per-axis alignment smart-guides still win; Alt disables).

fixedCanvas.description: Lock the canvas to render.width/height: the shell withholds setCanvasSize and ignores reserved ?width/?height, so box coordinates stay 1:1 with the render size (required when a hook draws into a fixed-viewBox overlay, e.g. connectors).

fields.description: Numeric sub-fields, each a labelled Figma-style scrubber. Stored as one compound value { fieldId: number } and rendered as a single control / column.

symbol.description: Single character shown inside the field as its scrub handle (e.g. "+" for zoom). Defaults to the first letter of the label.

exampleVariant.description: One example look: a set of input values (and optionally the UI theme it suits) rendered live to demonstrate the tool.

label.description: Short human label for this look (not shown to end users; documents the intent).

theme.description: Which UI theme this look suits - set only on looks that render ink on a TRANSPARENT background (e.g. a reverse/white logo). 'dark' looks show on the dark/SUSE themes, 'light' looks on the light theme; the clashing look is filtered out so it's never near-invisible on the tile. Omit for looks that bake their own background (shown on any theme).

values.description: Map of input id -> value seeded into the render - the same shape URL params resolve to. Scalar inputs (select/color/text/number/boolean/url) plus block arrays (e.g. chart data, badge tracks - an array of field objects) are supported; rely on the tool's default for asset inputs unless referencing a catalog asset id.

templateVariant.description: One named starting point in the "New from template" chooser: an id, a display name, and (in the external per-template file) a full input seed. Two shapes validate against this def: the EXTERNAL file tools/<id>/templates/<tid>.json, which carries `values`; and the METADATA-ONLY entry the synced index carries, which strips `values` (hence `values` is optional). Like an exampleVariant's `values` but read directly into a fresh session rather than rendered as an illustrative preview.

id.description: Stable id, unique within this tool's `templates[]`. Addressable via the reserved `?template=<id>` param, so treat it as a permanent contract like a tool/asset id.

name.description: Display name shown on the chooser tile.

description.description: Optional one-line description shown under the name on the tile.

category.description: Optional grouping label; tiles sharing a category are grouped together in the chooser.

thumb.description: Optional thumbnail: a tool-relative asset path or data URI. Absent → the chooser draws a glyph tile.

values.description: Map of input id -> value read directly into the fresh session - the same shape URL params resolve to, and the same shape a `default` composition uses. Authored in the EXTERNAL per-template file tools/<id>/templates/<tid>.json (not the synced index, which carries metadata only). Any size (a free-canvas `boxes` array can be many KB), because it is fetched on demand and seeded in-process, never serialised into a URL.
